boundary: A dated monitoring and response aid, not proof of suppression, diagnosis of any person, legal or medical advice, platform access, appeal-success assurance, or restored-distribution guarantee. Platform ranking and enforcement systems are opaque and change; reverify every policy, price, account surface, and decision before consequential use.

sources.title: Continuing our work to improve recommendations on YouTube
sources.claim: YouTube describes reducing recommendations of borderline content while leaving some content available.

sources.title: YouTube Community Guidelines
sources.claim: Removal and recommendation treatment are different events; inspect notices and analytics separately.

sources.title: Recommendation Guidelines
sources.claim: Meta applies a higher recommendation-eligibility standard than the standard for content allowed on its services.

sources.title: Policies
sources.claim: Meta publishes recommendation and community policies for Facebook and Instagram.

sources.title: Account Status and recommendation eligibility
sources.claim: Eligible professional accounts can inspect Account Status for recommendation eligibility; the surface does not prove why reach changed.

sources.title: For You feed eligibility standards
sources.claim: TikTok distinguishes content allowed on the service from content eligible for For You recommendation.

sources.title: Regulated goods and commercial activities
sources.claim: TikTok separately governs regulated goods, including drugs; exact scope and recommendation consequence require live verification.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework 1.0
sources.claim: NIST AI RMF organizes voluntary risk-management activity through Govern, Map, Measure, and Manage; its actions are not a universal checklist.
